sense: of a play, a film or a story

terms.gloss: the plot, the story of a play or a poem
terms.comment: The comic poets’ word: the prologue tells the argūmentum. Its other common senses are a proof and a piece of evidence (see argument, evidence); Quintilian notes that it means the subject matter of any piece of writing (Quint. 5.10.9).
The story itself, or the play (see play); not the plot as distinct from the play.

phrases.english: Next, don’t wait for the plot of the play

phrases.latin: Nōn ita dissimilī sunt argūmentō, sed tamen dissimilī ōrātiōne sunt factae ac stilō.
phrases.english: Their plots are not so different, but they are written in a different language and style.

phrases.latin: Līvius post aliquot annīs, quī ab saturīs ausus est prīmus argūmentō fābulam serere
phrases.english: Livius, some years later, who was the first to leave the saturae and dare to weave a play out of a plot
